When an option lets an AI tool change production, decide a rollback, or accept a refactor without measurement, it is almost always the distractor; the right answer gives the tool evidence and keeps verification deterministic.

quiz.q: An on-call team wants CloudWatch investigations to start automatically when the checkout-api-5xx alarm fires, to consider recent CloudTrail change events, and to be viewable and continuable by every on-call engineer. Investigations are currently started by hand with default settings. What should the developer configure?
choices: Nothing new, because default investigations already start on alarm state changes and are shared with every user who can read CloudWatch
An investigation group with its IAM role, CloudTrail management events sent to CloudWatch Logs in the same Region, and an investigation action on the alarm
A scheduled Lambda function that generates a Logs Insights query from a plain-English prompt every five minutes and emails the results
An export of all CloudTrail logs to an S3 bucket in us-east-1, because investigations read change events only from that Region's trail bucket
quiz.explain: The investigation group makes investigations shared and lets an alarm action start them, and trail events delivered to CloudWatch Logs in the same Region let investigations link errors to recent changes. Choice A fails because default investigations are user-started, private to that user and deleted after 24 hours.

quiz.q: Which pairing correctly matches a symptom to the first thing to check?
choices: API Gateway Latency is high while IntegrationLatency is low: the Lambda function's memory setting and its downstream DynamoDB calls
An ECS task stops with CannotPullContainerError: the container health check command and the binaries installed in the image
Lambda IteratorAge keeps rising on a Kinesis stream source: consumer throughput such as batch size, parallelization and function errors
A CloudFormation update shows twenty rollback events: the last UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE event, which holds the original failure reason
quiz.explain: Rising IteratorAge means records wait longer before processing, so the consumer is falling behind or retrying failures. Choice D is wrong because the original reason is in the first UPDATE_FAILED event; the rollback events that follow only describe the cleanup.

days.recap: Domain 4 in one line: read the signal that moved, query and trace to the failing layer, log and measure in structured and affordable ways, alert on quotas and deployment events, design honest health checks, optimize from evidence, and let AI tools explain and suggest while tests, metrics and people verify.

days.title: Final Day: Full Practice Exam, What Changed from DVA-C02 and Test-Day Checklist

concepts.heading: Exam Format and How to Pace It
concepts.body: DVA-C03 has 65 questions in 130 minutes: 50 scored and 15 unscored questions that you cannot tell apart, so treat every question as if it counts. The result is a scaled score from 100 to 1,000, and 720 passes. Questions are multiple choice (one answer) or multiple response (two or more answers, with the number stated). That gives two minutes per question; aim to finish a first pass in about 95 minutes, answering everything, flagging anything you are unsure of, and leaving time to revisit flags. Unanswered questions score as wrong, so never leave one blank. Take a full practice exam today under the same conditions, in one sitting, then review every miss and every lucky guess by writing down which keyword in the stem should have led you to the right answer.

concepts.heading: What Changed from DVA-C02
concepts.body: The four domains stay, but the weights move to Development with AWS Services 30 percent, Security 26 percent, Testing and Deployment 22 percent and Troubleshooting and Optimization 22 percent, compared with 32, 26, 24 and 18 in DVA-C02, so troubleshooting now carries more weight. New content centers on AI: AI-assisted development with Kiro (specs, steering files, agent hooks, code review and generated tests), integrating managed AI services such as Amazon Bedrock, Knowledge Bases and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and a new Security task on AI services covering model access, private connectivity, Guardrails, agent authorization and protecting prompts in logs. AI tools also appear inside testing, CI/CD and troubleshooting tasks. Container builds and deployments, from Dockerfiles and ECR to ECS, EKS and Fargate rollouts, now have explicit skills. The classic serverless core is unchanged.

concepts.heading: The Recurring Rule for AI Questions
concepts.body: Most AI-related options can be judged with one rule: AI generates, summarizes and explains, while deterministic controls decide. Tests with requirement-based assertions decide whether a build passes, not an AI summary. Fixed rules on a change set decide auto-approval, not a model's wording. CloudWatch alarms and CodeDeploy roll back a bad release, while CloudWatch investigations explains it afterwards. IAM and AgentCore policies limit what an agent can do, while Bedrock Guardrails filter content, not API calls, and a system prompt enforces nothing. AI output is treated like code: committed, reviewed and deployed by a scoped pipeline. Give AI tools rich but reduced context, and never give them production write access or long-term keys. Remember that Kiro and Amazon Bedrock are the in-scope tools; options built on tools outside the exam guide are rarely right.

concepts.heading: Confusable Pairs Worth a Final Pass
concepts.body: Spend the last review hours on pairs, not on new services. Domain 1: SQS versus SNS versus EventBridge, GSI versus LSI, Query versus Scan, Converse versus InvokeModel, lazy loading versus write-through. Domain 2: Cognito user pools versus identity pools, identity versus resource-based policies, S3 presigned URLs versus CloudFront signed cookies, Secrets Manager versus Parameter Store, SSE-KMS versus client-side encryption, Guardrails versus IAM. Domain 3: canary versus linear, change sets versus rollback triggers, stages versus aliases, minimumHealthyPercent versus maximumPercent, maxSurge versus maxUnavailable, IMMUTABLE versus IMMUTABLE_WITH_EXCLUSION. Domain 4: liveness versus readiness versus startup probes, EMF versus PutMetricData, reserved versus provisioned concurrency, ElastiCache versus DAX. For each pair, be able to name the one requirement word that picks one side.

concepts.heading: Test-Day Checklist
concepts.body: Confirm the appointment time and time zone, and for an online exam run the system check, clear the desk and have a valid ID that matches your registration name exactly. Sleep instead of cramming, and eat beforehand. During the exam, read the last sentence of each stem first to learn what is asked, then underline constraints such as least operational overhead, most cost-effective, without code changes or automatically. Eliminate options that break a stated constraint, then choose between the remaining two by the most specific requirement. For multiple response questions, choose exactly the number asked. Flag and move on after about two minutes. On the review pass, change an answer only when you find a concrete reason in the stem, not a feeling. Afterwards, note weak areas while they are fresh, whatever the result.

examPoints: A question that offers an AI tool as the decision-maker for a pass, an approval or a rollback is usually testing whether you keep deterministic controls in charge and use the AI tool for generation or explanation.
A question that hinges on a phrase such as least operational overhead, without code changes or automatically is testing whether you let that constraint eliminate otherwise workable options.

quiz.q: During the exam, a multiple-response question asks you to select TWO options. You are confident about one option and unsure between two others. What is the best approach?
choices: Select exactly two options, using the stem's constraints to choose between the uncertain ones, and flag the question for review
Select all three plausible options, because partial credit is given for each correct option chosen on multiple-response questions
Select only the confident option and leave the second choice empty so that a wrong guess cannot lower the score for the question
Skip the question without answering and plan to return to it only if time remains after every other question has been answered
quiz.explain: You must choose exactly the number of options requested, and unanswered or incomplete answers score as wrong, so pick the best second option and flag it. Choice B fails because selecting more options than requested makes the answer incorrect.

quiz.q: A practice question asks how to stop a CodeDeploy canary release of a Lambda function within minutes when errors rise, even at night, while the team also wants AI help understanding failures. Which answer matches the DVA-C03 pattern for AI questions?
choices: Disable automatic rollback and let a Lambda function ask a Bedrock model every minute whether the canary looks healthy before rolling back
Replace the PostTraffic hook with a prompt to a Bedrock model and report success whenever the model's answer does not mention an error
Keep the faulty version live during business hours so that a Kiro agent can analyze the production errors and write a fix before the canary ends
Attach CloudWatch alarms to the deployment for automatic rollback, and add an investigation action to the same alarms to start a CloudWatch investigation
quiz.explain: Alarms on the deployment give a deterministic, unattended rollback, and the same alarms can start a CloudWatch investigation so AI-generated hypotheses are ready afterwards. Choice A makes rollback depend on a model's judgment of log text, which can be slow or wrong.

days.recap: Take one timed full practice exam, review every miss by its keyword, remember the new DVA-C03 weights and AI, AI-security and container content, apply the rule that AI explains while deterministic controls decide, drill confusable pairs, and walk in rested with a pacing plan of about two minutes per question.
